Drives reporting buckets for shrinkage monitoring, COGS (Cost of Goods Sold) impact analysis, and loss prevention dashboards. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: shrinkage|damage|cycle_count_correction|receiving_variance|expiry_write_off|rtv|admin_correction|found_stock — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: reason_sub_category
attributes.description: Granular sub-classification within the reason category providing specific cause detail. Examples for shrinkage: shoplifting, employee theft, administrative error, vendor fraud. Examples for damage: in-transit damage, handling damage, shelf damage. Feeds loss prevention case analysis and shrinkage root-cause reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: shoplifting|employee_theft|admin_error|vendor_fraud|in_transit_damage|handling_damage|shelf_damage|expired|recalled|mis-ship — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: recall_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this inventory adjustment is associated with a product recall event initiated by the CPSC, FDA, or the retailer. Enables rapid identification and financial quantification of recall-related inventory write-offs.

attributes.name: rfid_tag_count
attributes.description: Number of RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) tags scanned during the detection event that triggered this adjustment. Populated only for RFID-based detection methods. Supports RFID program accuracy measurement and tag read-rate analysis.

attributes.name: source_document_number
attributes.description: The reference number of the originating source document (e.g., cycle count ID, RTV authorization number, receiving document number, damage report ID). Enables cross-system traceability and audit trail linkage.

attributes.name: source_document_type
attributes.description: The type of source business document that triggered or supports this inventory adjustment. Provides traceability back to the originating business process (e.g., cycle count sheet, Return to Vendor (RTV) authorization, receiving document). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: cycle_count|physical_inventory|rtv_authorization|receiving_document|damage_report|expiry_report|pos_exception_report — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: unit_cost
attributes.description: The Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) per unit at the time of adjustment, used to calculate the total cost impact of the inventory change. Sourced from the inventory valuation layer in SAP S/4HANA. Business-confidential as it reflects supplier pricing.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System audit timestamp recording when the adjustment record was most recently modified. Tracks approval workflow updates, status changes, and corrections. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

products.name: stock_transfer
products.description: Inter-node stock transfer records capturing movement of inventory between stores, DCs, MFCs, and vendor locations. Captures transfer type (store-to-store, DC-to-store, cross-dock, RTV), source node, destination node, SKU, transfer quantity, shipment date, expected receipt date, actual receipt date, carrier, and transfer status. Supports omnichannel fulfillment (ship-from-store) and network balancing.

attributes.name: stock_transfer_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated surrogate identifier for each inter-node stock transfer record in the inventory management system.

attributes.name: carrier_id
attributes.description: Reference to the logistics carrier or 3PL (Third-Party Logistics) provider responsible for transporting the stock transfer between nodes. Used for carrier performance analytics and SLA compliance reporting.

attributes.name: cost_price_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pricing.cost_price. Business justification: Transfer accounting and intercompany pricing require cost data for inventory valuation during movement. Store-to-store transfers, DC-to-store shipments, and cross-dock operations need cost basis for f

attributes.name: destination_node_inventory_node_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the receiving inventory node (store, DC, MFC, or vendor location) to which the stock transfer is directed. Used for inventory receipt confirmation and network replenishment tracking.

attributes.name: lot_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to inventory.lot. Business justification: Inter-node stock transfers frequently move specific lots, particularly for perishable or lot-tracked items where FEFO sequencing and expiry management require lot-level transfer tracking. Adding lot_i

attributes.name: order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fulfillment.fulfillment_order. Business justification: Ship-from-store and store-to-store transfers are initiated to fulfill specific fulfillment orders (BOPIS, ROPIS, SFS). Linking stock_transfer to fulfillment_order enables end-to-end order fulfillment

attributes.name: order_line_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to order.order_line. Business justification: Ship-from-store fulfillment: when an online order line triggers a store-to-customer transfer, the stock_transfer must reference the originating order_line for customer service tracing, SLA compliance

attributes.name: outbound_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supplychain.outbound_order. Business justification: DC-to-store transfer execution: a stock_transfer (inventory movement record) corresponds to an outbound_order (DC shipping execution record). Retail inventory and DC operations teams need this link fo

attributes.name: primary_stock_inventory_node_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the originating inventory node (store, DC, MFC, or vendor location) from which the stock transfer is dispatched. Supports network balancing and omnichannel fulfillment analytics.

attributes.name: promo_campaign_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to promotion.promo_campaign. Business justification: Retailers execute targeted inter-store and DC-to-store transfers to concentrate promotional stock at high-traffic locations before campaign launch. Linking stock_transfer to promo_campaign enables pro

attributes.name: purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the originating purchase order that triggered this stock transfer, applicable for DC-to-store replenishment flows sourced from supplier inbound receipts. Links transfer to procurement context.

attributes.name: replenishment_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to inventory.replenishment_order. Business justification: A stock transfer is frequently initiated to fulfill a replenishment order — moving inventory from a DC to a store or between nodes as directed by the replenishment system. Linking stock_transfer to re

attributes.name: replenishment_plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the replenishment plan that generated this stock transfer, linking the physical movement to the demand-driven planning signal from Blue Yonder or Oracle Retail. Supports replenishment accuracy analytics.

attributes.name: shipment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fulfillment.shipment. Business justification: Inter-node stock transfers that are physically shipped generate carrier shipments. Linking stock_transfer to shipment enables tracking number association, carrier cost allocation to transfer events, a

attributes.name: sku_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) being transferred. The SKU is the atomic unit of inventory tracking, uniquely identifying a product variant (size, color, style) within the retail assortment.

attributes.name: uom_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.uom. Business justification: stock_transfer.unit_of_measure is a denormalized text field. Inter-node transfers require validated UOM for transfer_cost calculations, receiving reconciliation, and variance_quantity reporting — all

attributes.name: actual_receipt_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the stock transfer was physically received and confirmed at the destination node. Compared against expected_receipt_date to measure carrier and DC performance against SLA targets.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System audit timestamp recording when this stock transfer record was first persisted in the data platform. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and Silver layer ingestion tracking.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the transfer cost is denominated (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR). Supports multi-currency retail operations across international markets.

attributes.name: destination_node_type
attributes.description: Classification of the receiving inventory node. STORE: retail store; DC: distribution center; MFC: micro-fulfillment center; VENDOR: supplier location for RTV; DARK_STORE: fulfillment-only location.

attributes.name: expected_receipt_date
attributes.description: Planned calendar date by which the stock transfer is expected to arrive at the destination node. Used for replenishment planning, weeks of supply (WOS) calculations, and SLA compliance monitoring.

attributes.name: initiated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the stock transfer record was first created in the system, representing the business event of transfer initiation. Serves as the principal business event timestamp for the transfer lifecycle.

attributes.name: inventory_cost_per_unit
attributes.business_glossary_term: Inventory Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) Per Unit
attributes.description: Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) value per unit for the transferred SKU at time of transfer, used for inventory valuation, GMROI calculations, and financial reporting. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA FI/CO standard cost or moving average cost.

tag_set.value: Inventory Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) Per Unit

attributes.name: is_cross_dock
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this stock transfer is executed as a cross-docking (cross-dock) movement, where inventory is transferred directly from inbound to outbound at the DC without putaway storage. Supports DC throughput and flow-through analytics.

attributes.name: is_ship_from_store
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this stock transfer is part of a ship-from-store (SFS) omnichannel fulfillment flow, where a retail store acts as a fulfillment node dispatching inventory to satisfy an e-commerce or BOPIS order.

attributes.name: is_vendor_managed
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this stock transfer is part of a Vendor Managed Inventory (VMI) program, where the supplier initiates and manages the replenishment transfer rather than the retailer's internal planning team.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text operational notes or comments associated with the stock transfer, capturing exception details, special handling instructions, or carrier communication relevant to the transfer execution.

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Operational priority assigned to the stock transfer, influencing pick sequencing, carrier selection, and dispatch scheduling at the DC or store. URGENT transfers may be triggered by stockout alerts or product recalls.

attributes.name: received_quantity
attributes.description: Actual number of units confirmed received at the destination node upon delivery. May differ from transfer_quantity due to transit damage, shrinkage, or carrier discrepancies. Drives inventory reconciliation and shrinkage monitoring.

attributes.name: rfid_enabled
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this stock transfer was tracked using RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) technology for real-time inventory visibility during transit. Supports RFID-based inventory accuracy programs.

attributes.name: shipment_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the stock transfer was physically dispatched from the source node. Used for lead time calculation, carrier SLA tracking, and inventory in-transit reporting.

attributes.name: source_node_type
attributes.description: Classification of the originating inventory node. STORE: retail store; DC: distribution center; MFC: micro-fulfillment center; VENDOR: supplier location for RTV or DSD; DARK_STORE: fulfillment-only location.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this stock transfer record originated. Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and Silver layer provenance tracking across the retail technology stack.

attributes.name: tracking_number
attributes.description: Carrier-assigned shipment tracking number for the stock transfer, enabling real-time in-transit visibility and last-mile delivery monitoring. Used for exception management and carrier SLA validation.

attributes.name: transfer_cost
attributes.description: Total logistics cost incurred for executing this stock transfer, including carrier freight charges, handling fees, and any 3PL surcharges. Used for inventory valuation (COGS), P&L allocation, and supply chain cost optimization.

attributes.name: transfer_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business reference number for the stock transfer, used for tracking and communication across supply chain partners, carriers, and store operations. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA MM transfer order numbering.

attributes.name: transfer_quantity
attributes.description: Number of units of the SKU authorized and dispatched in this stock transfer. Represents the planned transfer quantity as recorded at time of transfer creation.

attributes.name: transfer_reason_code
attributes.description: Business reason code explaining why the stock transfer was initiated. REPLENISHMENT: routine inventory restocking; NETWORK_BALANCE: lateral balancing to address overstock/understock; RTV: return to vendor; RECALL: product safety recall per CPSC; DAMAGE_RETURN: return of damaged goods; OMNICHANNEL: ship-from-store or BOPIS fulfillment support.

attributes.name: transfer_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the stock transfer. DRAFT: initiated but not yet dispatched; IN_TRANSIT: shipment dispatched from source node; RECEIVED: confirmed receipt at destination node; CANCELLED: transfer voided before completion; EXCEPTION: discrepancy or damage reported during transit.

attributes.name: transfer_type
attributes.description: Classification of the inter-node inventory movement. DC_TO_STORE: distribution center replenishment to store; STORE_TO_STORE: lateral balancing between stores; STORE_TO_DC: reverse logistics or consolidation; CROSS_DOCK: direct transfer without storage per cross-docking (DSD) model; RTV: Return to Vendor; MFC_TO_STORE: micro-fulfillment center to store for omnichannel fulfillment (ship-from-store).

attributes.name: upc
attributes.description: 12-digit Universal Product Code (UPC) barcode identifier for the transferred SKU, used for scanning and verification during pick, pack, and receipt operations at DC and store nodes.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System audit timestamp recording the most recent modification to this stock transfer record, such as status updates, quantity adjustments, or receipt confirmations. Supports change data capture and audit compliance.

attributes.name: variance_quantity
attributes.description: Difference between transfer_quantity and received_quantity, representing units lost, damaged, or unaccounted for during transit. Positive value indicates shortage; negative indicates overage. Drives shrinkage monitoring and carrier chargeback processes.

attributes.name: variance_reason_code
attributes.description: Reason code explaining the cause of any quantity variance between dispatched and received units. Used for shrinkage root cause analysis, carrier chargeback (RMA) processing, and inventory reconciliation.

products.name: goods_receipt
products.description: Records physical receipt of merchandise at DCs, stores, and MFCs against purchase orders, replenishment orders, or transfer orders. Captures receipt date, receiving node, supplier/source, PO/ASN reference, line-level received/accepted/rejected quantities with discrepancy details (shortage, overage, wrong SKU, damage), unit cost, receipt method (DSD, DC-to-store, cross-dock), quality inspection status, and discrepancy resolution status. Supports receiving workflows, vendor compliance chargebacks, and inventory accuracy at point of induction.

attributes.name: goods_receipt_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated surrogate identifier for each goods receipt record in the inventory domain. Primary key for the goods_receipt data product.

attributes.name: cost_price_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pricing.cost_price. Business justification: Receiving process validates invoice costs against contracted pricing and updates landed cost. Three-way match (PO-receipt-invoice) depends on linking goods receipt to cost structure for variance detec

attributes.name: inbound_shipment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supplychain.inbound_shipment. Business justification: ASN-to-receipt matching: goods_receipt is the inventory confirmation of an inbound_shipment's arrival. Retail receiving teams match ASNs to receipts for discrepancy resolution. bill_of_lading_number a

attributes.name: inventory_node_id
attributes.description: Reference to the physical location (DC, store, or MFC) where the merchandise was received. Supports inventory accuracy at point of induction and omnichannel fulfillment visibility.

attributes.name: po_line_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific purchase order line item being received. Enables line-level PO matching, partial receipt tracking, and SKU-level discrepancy analysis.

attributes.name: purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent purchase order against which this goods receipt is posted. Enables PO-to-receipt matching, open order tracking, and three-way match (PO, receipt, invoice) for accounts payable.

attributes.name: receiving_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supplychain.receiving_event. Business justification: DC receiving process: receiving_event is the physical unloading/inspection event; goods_receipt is the inventory system record created from it. Retail DC managers need to link these for quality inspec

attributes.name: replenishment_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to inventory.replenishment_order. Business justification: A goods receipt records the physical arrival of merchandise against a replenishment order (in addition to purchase orders). goods_receipt already has purchase_order_id for PO-based receipts, but lacks

attributes.name: sku_id
attributes.description: Reference to the SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) being received. Links to the product master in Informatica MDM or Oracle Retail Merchandising System for item-level inventory induction.

attributes.name: uom_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.uom. Business justification: goods_receipt.unit_of_measure is a denormalized text field. Goods receipt drives total_receipt_cost and discrepancy calculations; linking to product.uom ensures received quantities are validated again

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Reference to the supplier or vendor from whom the merchandise was received. Links to the supplier master record in Informatica MDM. Used for vendor compliance chargeback processing and fill rate analysis.

attributes.name: vendor_item_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supplier.vendor_item. Business justification: Receiving teams validate received goods against the vendor's item catalog (pack size, GTIN, unit cost). Linking goods_receipt to vendor_item enables discrepancy detection and chargeback eligibility as

attributes.name: vendor_promo_agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to promotion.vendor_promo_agreement. Business justification: Vendor promotional agreements specify promotional purchase quantities and delivery obligations. Linking goods receipts to vendor_promo_agreement enables performance obligation tracking, chargeback rec

attributes.name: accepted_qty
attributes.description: Quantity of units accepted into inventory after quality inspection. Excludes rejected, damaged, or wrong-SKU units. This is the quantity inducted into on-hand inventory and used for COGS valuation.

attributes.name: chargeback_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this goods receipt record has identified discrepancies that qualify for a vendor compliance chargeback. True = chargeback may be issued to supplier; False = no chargeback applicable. Drives the vendor compliance chargeback workflow.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System audit timestamp recording when this goods receipt record was first created in the data platform. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and SLA monitoring.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the unit cost and total receipt cost (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for multi-currency retail operations and financial reporting.

attributes.name: discrepancy_resolution_status
attributes.description: Current status of the discrepancy resolution workflow. 'pending' = discrepancy logged, not yet actioned; 'under_review' = being investigated with supplier; 'resolved' = discrepancy closed; 'chargeback_issued' = vendor compliance chargeback raised; 'waived' = discrepancy accepted without penalty.

attributes.name: discrepancy_type
attributes.description: Classification of the primary discrepancy identified during receiving. 'shortage' = fewer units than expected; 'overage' = more units than expected; 'wrong_sku' = incorrect item received; 'damage' = merchandise physically damaged; 'expired' = past sell-by or use-by date; 'none' = no discrepancy. Drives chargeback and resolution workflows.

attributes.name: expected_qty
attributes.description: Quantity of units expected at the receiving node based on the ASN or replenishment plan. May differ from ordered quantity due to partial shipments or split deliveries. Used for receiving dock planning and discrepancy detection.

attributes.name: inspection_date
attributes.description: Date on which the quality inspection of received merchandise was completed. Used for compliance reporting, CPSC/FDA audit trails, and receiving cycle time analysis.

attributes.name: ordered_qty
attributes.description: Quantity of units originally ordered on the purchase order line. Used as the baseline for receipt variance calculation, fill rate measurement, and vendor compliance scoring.

attributes.name: overage_qty
attributes.description: Quantity of units received in excess of the ASN or PO expectation (received_qty minus expected_qty when positive). Overages require disposition decisions and may trigger vendor compliance chargebacks.

attributes.name: po_number
attributes.description: Externally-known purchase order number as referenced on supplier documentation and EDI transactions. Retained for operational readability, vendor communication, and three-way match without requiring a join.

attributes.name: quality_inspection_status
attributes.description: Status of the quality inspection performed on received merchandise. 'not_required' = inspection waived per supplier agreement; 'pending' = awaiting inspection; 'passed' = all units meet quality standards; 'failed' = units do not meet standards; 'partial_pass' = some units accepted, some rejected. Drives accepted/rejected quantity split.

attributes.name: receipt_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the physical goods receipt was posted. Used for inventory valuation, vendor compliance reporting, and lead time analysis. Aligns with SAP Posting Date (BUDAT) in the MM module.

attributes.name: receipt_method
attributes.description: Method by which merchandise was physically received. 'dsd' = Direct Store Delivery from supplier; 'dc_to_store' = replenishment from Distribution Center; 'cross_dock' = direct transfer without storage; 'drop_ship' = vendor direct-to-customer; 'transfer_order' = inter-node stock transfer. Drives receiving workflow and inventory valuation logic.

attributes.name: receipt_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes entered by the receiving associate documenting special conditions, discrepancy details, handling instructions, or other observations at the time of receipt. Supports discrepancy investigation and vendor communication.

attributes.name: receipt_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the goods receipt document, typically generated by the WMS or ERP upon physical receipt confirmation. Maps to SAP Material Document Number (MBLNR) or Manhattan WMS Receipt Number.

attributes.name: receipt_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the goods receipt workflow. 'draft' indicates initiated but not confirmed; 'open' indicates awaiting physical receipt; 'in_progress' indicates receiving underway; 'completed' indicates fully processed and inventory inducted; 'cancelled' indicates voided; 'on_hold' indicates paused pending resolution. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|open|in_progress|completed|cancelled|on_hold — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: receipt_timestamp
attributes.description: The principal real-world event timestamp recording when the physical merchandise was received and confirmed at the receiving node (DC, store, or MFC). Distinct from system audit timestamps. Maps to SAP Posting Date/Time in MIGO.

attributes.name: received_qty
attributes.description: Total quantity of units physically counted and received at the dock, prior to quality inspection. Includes all units regardless of condition. Used as the gross receipt quantity for inventory induction and discrepancy calculation.

attributes.name: receiving_node_type
attributes.description: Classification of the physical location type where goods were received. 'dc' = Distribution Center; 'store' = retail store; 'mfc' = Micro-Fulfillment Center; 'dark_store' = fulfillment-only location. Determines applicable receiving workflows and inventory induction rules.

attributes.name: rejected_qty
attributes.description: Quantity of units rejected during quality inspection and not inducted into inventory. Drives Return to Vendor (RTV) processing, vendor compliance chargebacks, and RMA initiation.

attributes.name: rfid_verified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the received merchandise was verified using RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) scanning during the receiving process. True = RFID scan confirmed; False = manual or barcode-only verification. Supports inventory accuracy at point of induction.

attributes.name: rtv_initiated
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Return to Vendor (RTV) process has been initiated for rejected units from this goods receipt. True = RTV in progress; False = no RTV initiated. Supports reverse logistics and vendor debit memo processing.

attributes.name: shortage_qty
attributes.description: Quantity of units short-shipped relative to the ASN or PO expectation (expected_qty minus received_qty when negative). Used for vendor compliance chargeback calculation and fill rate reporting.

attributes.name: total_receipt_cost
attributes.description: Total cost of accepted merchandise received (accepted_qty × unit_cost). Used for inventory valuation, COGS posting, and financial reconciliation. Classified as confidential due to commercial sensitivity.

attributes.name: unit_cost
attributes.description: Cost per unit of the received merchandise as per the purchase order or supplier invoice. Used for inventory valuation (COGS), gross margin calculation (GMROI), and financial posting to the general ledger. Classified as confidential due to commercial sensitivity.

attributes.name: upc
attributes.description: 12-digit Universal Product Code (UPC) barcode identifier for the received item. Used for RFID/barcode scanning during receiving, inventory accuracy validation, and GS1 compliance.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System audit timestamp recording when this goods receipt record was last modified in the data platform. Supports change tracking, discrepancy resolution audits, and data quality monitoring.

products.name: reservation

Single source of truth for all reserved and held stock, enabling accurate ATP calculation on stock_position.

attributes.description: System identifier for the SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) whose inventory is being reserved or held. Links to the product master for item-level ATP (Available to Promise) calculation and omnichannel fulfillment routing.

attributes.name: stock_position_id
attributes.description: Reference to the stock_position record at the SKU-node level that this reservation encumbers. Enables direct linkage between the reservation and the ATP calculation on the stock_position product, ensuring accurate real-time inventory visibility.

attributes.description: Name or code of the business department that authorized the hold (e.g., Quality Assurance, Legal, Compliance, Store Operations, E-Commerce Fulfillment). Supports departmental accountability reporting and hold resolution workflows.

attributes.name: case_reference_number
attributes.description: Reference to the service case, quality investigation, legal matter, or regulatory recall case that authorized a hard hold. Populated for quality_hold, legal_hold, regulatory_recall, and damage_hold encumbrance types. Links to Salesforce Service Cloud case management.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System-generated timestamp when the reservation record was first written to the data platform (Silver layer ingestion time). Distinct from reservation_timestamp which captures the business event time. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the inventory_cost_per_unit value (e.g., USD, CAD, GBP). Supports multi-currency inventory valuation for international retail operations.

attributes.name: encumbrance_type
attributes.description: Classifies the nature of the inventory encumbrance. Critical for BOPIS and e-commerce holds where stock must be released back to general availability after a defined window (e.g., 24–48 hours). Null for indefinite holds such as legal or regulatory holds.

attributes.name: fiscal_period
attributes.description: Retail fiscal period (year and period number, e.g., 2024-P07) during which the reservation was created. Supports financial reporting of encumbered inventory valuation, OTB (Open to Buy) impact analysis, and period-end inventory reconciliation per FASB ASC 330.

attributes.name: fulfillment_channel
attributes.description: The omnichannel fulfillment method associated with this reservation. BOPIS (Buy Online Pick Up In Store), ROPIS (Reserve Online Pick Up In Store), ship_from_store (SFS), ecommerce (ship from DC), drop_ship (vendor direct), in_store (POS hold). Null for non-order-driven hard holds.

attributes.name: hold_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the specific business reason for the reservation or hold (e.g., BOPIS_ALLOC, SFS_ALLOC, ECOM_HOLD, QA_FAIL, RECALL_CPSC, LEGAL_HOLD, DMG_INBOUND, PRICE_INVEST). Enables operational reporting and root-cause analysis of inventory encumbrances.

attributes.name: hold_reason_description

attributes.name: inventory_cost_per_unit
attributes.description: Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) per unit for the reserved SKU at the time of reservation creation. Used for financial valuation of encumbered inventory, shrinkage reporting, and GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Investment) analysis. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA Retail FI/CO module.

attributes.name: is_recalled
attributes.description: Indicates whether this reservation was created in response to a regulatory product recall (CPSC, FDA, or other governing body). When true, the hold cannot be released without explicit compliance authorization. Supports mandatory recall reporting and quarantine workflows.

attributes.name: is_vendor_managed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the reserved inventory is managed under a Vendor Managed Inventory (VMI) agreement, where the supplier retains ownership and replenishment responsibility. Affects financial liability and hold authorization workflows.

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Business priority assigned to the reservation, governing queue position in fulfillment workflows and hold resolution SLAs. 'critical' applies to regulatory recalls and legal holds; 'high' to same-day BOPIS; 'standard' to regular e-commerce holds; 'low' to pre-emptive soft allocations.

attributes.name: release_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing resolution details, disposition instructions, or compliance notes recorded at the time of hold release. Required for regulatory recalls and legal holds to document the resolution rationale for audit purposes.

attributes.name: release_status
attributes.description: Approval workflow status for releasing a hard hold. 'pending' — release request submitted awaiting authorization; 'approved' — release authorized by responsible department; 'rejected' — release denied, hold remains active; 'auto_released' — system-triggered release upon expiry or order fulfillment; 'escalated' — requires senior authorization.

attributes.name: release_timestamp
attributes.description: Actual date and time when the reservation was released, cancelled, or converted. Null while the reservation is active. Used for hold duration analysis, SLA compliance reporting, and ATP recalculation upon release.

attributes.name: reservation_number
attributes.description: Externally-visible, human-readable business identifier for the reservation, used in operational communications, order management, and customer-facing references (e.g., BOPIS confirmation codes). Sourced from OMS or WMS upon creation.

attributes.name: reservation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the inventory reservation. 'active' — stock is currently encumbered; 'expired' — reservation lapsed past expiry without fulfillment; 'released' — hold manually or systematically lifted; 'cancelled' — reservation voided before fulfillment; 'pending_release' — awaiting authorization to release; 'converted' — soft allocation fulfilled and converted to a shipment.

attributes.name: reservation_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (with timezone offset) when the inventory encumbrance was created — the principal business event timestamp. For BOPIS/e-commerce holds, this is when the customer completed checkout. For quality/legal holds, this is when the hold was authorized.

attributes.name: reserved_quantity
attributes.description: Number of units of the SKU encumbered by this reservation. Subtracted from on-hand quantity to derive ATP (Available to Promise) on the stock_position product. Must be positive and not exceed available on-hand at time of reservation creation.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record that originated this reservation record (e.g., WMS = Manhattan Associates WMS, OMS = Order Management System, ECOM = Salesforce Commerce Cloud, ERP = SAP S/4HANA, MANUAL = manually entered hold). Supports data lineage and reconciliation in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver layer. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WMS|OMS|ECOM|ERP|ORMS|CAR|SFCC|MANUAL — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: storage_bin
attributes.description: Specific bin, shelf, or slot location within the node where the reserved inventory is physically stored. Enables warehouse associates to locate and pick reserved stock efficiently. Sourced from Manhattan Associates WMS bin management.

attributes.name: upc
attributes.description: 12-digit Universal Product Code (UPC) barcode identifier for the reserved item. Used for RFID scanning, POS reconciliation, and regulatory recall identification per GS1 standards.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System-generated timestamp of the most recent modification to the reservation record (e.g., quantity adjustment, status change, expiry extension). Used for change data capture (CDC) and incremental processing in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver layer.

products.name: reorder_policy

Trigger thresholds generate inventory_replenishment_order records when stock_position breaches defined levels. Owned and maintained by replenishment planners; consumed by automated replenishment engines.

attributes.name: reorder_policy_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the reorder policy record. Primary key for the reorder_policy data product in the inventory domain.

attributes.name: cluster_id

attributes.name: demand_forecast_id

attributes.name: department_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to store.department. Business justification: Reorder policies in retail are scoped to a specific department within a store (e.g., Produce has different min/max rules than Electronics). Department-level replenishment policy management is a standa

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to inventory.inventory_node. attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.item_hierarchy. Business justification: Retail replenishment planning sets policies at category/hierarchy level (item_hierarchy.replenishment_method, safety_stock_weeks). A reorder_policy can govern all SKUs in a hierarchy node, enabling ca

attributes.name: promo_calendar_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to promotion.promo_calendar. Business justification: Reorder policies are adjusted for promotional periods defined in the promo_calendar (safety stock uplift, lead time compression). Linking reorder_policy to promo_calendar enables promotional replenish

attributes.description: Reference to the parent replenishment plan that governs or generated this reorder policy. Links the policy to the broader supply chain planning context managed in Blue Yonder Demand Planning.

attributes.name: sku_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) for which this reorder policy applies. Combined with location_id, forms the natural business key for a reorder policy.

attributes.name: uom_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.uom. Business justification: reorder_policy.unit_of_measure is a denormalized text field. Reorder point quantities, MOQ, and safety stock quantities must reference the authoritative UOM to ensure replenishment calculations are co

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Reference to the preferred supplier for replenishment orders generated by this policy. Used by the replenishment engine to route purchase orders. May be overridden at order generation time if the supplier is unavailable.

attributes.name: vendor_item_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supplier.vendor_item. Business justification: Reorder policies are configured per SKU-vendor combination using vendor_item pack size, MOQ, and order increment. Linking reorder_policy to vendor_item enables automatic policy recalculation when vend

attributes.name: abc_classification
attributes.description: ABC classification of the SKU at this location based on sales velocity and revenue contribution: A (high-velocity/high-value), B (medium), C (low-velocity/low-value), D (dead stock or near-dead). Influences replenishment priority, safety stock levels, and review cycle frequency.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the replenishment planner or manager who approved this reorder policy for activation. Supports governance, audit trail, and accountability for policy parameters.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this reorder policy was formally approved for activation by the authorized planner or manager. Supports audit trail and policy lifecycle management.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this reorder policy record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and policy lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The calendar date from which this reorder policy becomes active and the replenishment engine begins applying its parameters. Supports time-bound policy management and seasonal policy transitions.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The calendar date after which this reorder policy is no longer active. Null indicates an open-ended policy with no planned expiration. Used to manage seasonal policies, promotional replenishment windows, and policy version transitions.

attributes.name: is_auto_replenishment
attributes.description: Indicates whether replenishment orders are automatically generated and submitted when the reorder trigger is breached (True), or whether a replenishment planner must manually review and approve the suggested order (False).

attributes.name: is_seasonal
attributes.description: Indicates whether this reorder policy applies seasonal adjustments to replenishment parameters (e.g., elevated safety stock or WOS targets during peak seasons). When True, seasonal override parameters may be applied by the replenishment engine.

attributes.name: is_vendor_managed
attributes.description: Indicates whether this SKU-location replenishment is managed by the supplier under a Vendor Managed Inventory (VMI) agreement. When True, the supplier is responsible for monitoring stock levels and initiating replenishment orders rather than the retailer's automated engine.

attributes.name: last_reviewed_date
attributes.description: The most recent date on which a replenishment planner reviewed and validated the parameters of this reorder policy. Supports governance and audit of policy maintenance cadence.

attributes.name: lead_time_days
attributes.description: The expected number of calendar days from placement of a replenishment purchase order to receipt of goods at the destination location. Used to calculate the reorder point and ensure stock does not fall below safety stock during the replenishment cycle.

attributes.name: location_type
attributes.description: Classification of the inventory node type to which this policy applies: store (retail store), DC (Distribution Center), MFC (Micro-Fulfillment Center), dark_store (fulfillment-only location), or warehouse. Drives replenishment logic differences by node type.

attributes.name: max_stock_quantity
attributes.description: The maximum allowable on-hand inventory level (in units) for this SKU at this location. Used in min/max reorder method as the upper bound. Replenishment orders are sized to bring stock up to this level without exceeding it.

attributes.name: min_stock_quantity
attributes.description: The minimum allowable on-hand inventory level (in units) for this SKU at this location. Used in min/max reorder method as the lower bound. Stock falling below this level triggers an urgent replenishment order.

attributes.name: moq
attributes.description: The minimum number of units that must be ordered per replenishment order as stipulated by the supplier contract. Replenishment engine enforces this floor when generating inventory_replenishment_order records.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date for the next planner review of this reorder policy's parameters. Calculated from last_reviewed_date plus the review_cycle_days. Drives planner workqueue prioritization.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for replenishment planners to document rationale for policy parameter choices, exceptions, seasonal considerations, or supplier-specific constraints associated with this reorder policy.

attributes.name: order_multiple
attributes.business_glossary_term: Order Multiple (Case Pack / Minimum Order Quantity)
attributes.description: The quantity increment in which orders must be placed, reflecting the supplier's case pack size or Minimum Order Quantity (MOQ). All replenishment order quantities are rounded up to the nearest multiple of this value to comply with supplier constraints.

attributes.name: order_quantity
attributes.description: The fixed quantity (in units) to order each time a replenishment trigger is activated. Used for fixed_quantity reorder method. For other methods, this field may be null and the order quantity is dynamically calculated.

attributes.name: policy_code
attributes.description: Business-facing unique alphanumeric code identifying the reorder policy, used by replenishment planners and referenced in automated replenishment engines (e.g., Blue Yonder). Externally visible identifier across systems.

attributes.name: policy_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name for the reorder policy, used by replenishment planners to identify and manage policies (e.g., 'DC Grocery Min/Max Weekly', 'Store Electronics WOS-Based').

attributes.name: policy_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the reorder policy. Controls whether the policy is actively used by the replenishment engine to generate inventory_replenishment_order records. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|inactive|draft|pending_approval|expired|suspended — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: policy_version
attributes.description: Incrementing version number for this reorder policy record, incremented each time parameters are materially changed. Supports policy change history tracking and rollback capability for replenishment planners.

attributes.name: reorder_method
attributes.description: The replenishment calculation method applied by this policy: min_max (reorder when stock falls below minimum, order up to maximum), days_of_supply (maintain a target number of days of inventory), wos_based (Weeks of Supply (WOS) target), forecast_driven (demand forecast from Blue Yonder), fixed_quantity (constant order quantity), vendor_managed (VMI — Vendor Managed Inventory where supplier controls replenishment). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: min_max|days_of_supply|wos_based|forecast_driven|fixed_quantity|vendor_managed — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: reorder_point_quantity
attributes.description: The on-hand stock level (in units) at which a replenishment order is automatically triggered. When the stock_position in inventory falls at or below this threshold, an inventory_replenishment_order record is generated. Core parameter for min/max and fixed-quantity reorder methods.

attributes.name: review_cycle_days
attributes.description: The frequency in calendar days at which the replenishment engine evaluates this policy and checks whether a reorder trigger has been breached. Defines the periodic review interval (e.g., daily=1, weekly=7, bi-weekly=14).

attributes.name: safety_stock_quantity
attributes.description: Buffer stock quantity (in units) maintained above the reorder point to protect against demand variability and supply lead time uncertainty. Prevents stockouts during replenishment cycles. A key input to the reorder point calculation.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this reorder policy was originated or last updated: ORMS (Oracle Retail Merchandising System), SAP_MM (SAP S/4HANA MM Module), BLUE_YONDER (Blue Yonder Demand Planning), MANUAL (planner-entered), MDM (Informatica MDM). Supports data lineage in the Databricks Silver Layer.

attributes.name: target_days_of_supply
attributes.description: The desired number of days of inventory coverage to maintain at this location for this SKU. Used in days_of_supply reorder method to calculate the replenishment order quantity based on forecasted daily demand.

attributes.name: target_wos
attributes.description: The desired number of weeks of inventory coverage (Weeks of Supply — WOS) to maintain at this location for this SKU. Used in wos_based reorder method. Replenishment orders are sized to achieve this WOS target based on forecasted weekly demand.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this reorder policy record was most recently modified. Tracks parameter changes made by replenishment planners and supports change audit trails.

products.name: contact
products.description: Stores all contact points for a customer profile or corporate account including email addresses, phone numbers, and social handles. Each row represents a single contact method with type (primary email, mobile, work phone, WhatsApp), verification status, opt-in/opt-out flags per channel, verification date, and source system. Supports omnichannel outreach, CRM campaigns via the case management system, and GDPR/CCPA consent enforcement at the contact-method level. Deployed to retail_mvm (MVM) and retail_mvm (ECM) as distinct schemas.

attributes.name: contact_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the contact method record. Primary key.

attributes.name: profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer profile or corporate account that owns this contact method. Links to the customer master record in the customer master data system.

attributes.name: bounce_count
attributes.description: The cumulative number of times communication attempts via this contact method have bounced or failed. Used to trigger contact validation workflows and suppress invalid addresses.

attributes.name: consent_source
attributes.description: The channel or touchpoint where the customer provided consent for this contact method (e.g., web registration, mobile app, POS, call center, in-store signup). attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the contact method. Active indicates usable for communication; bounced/invalid indicates delivery failure; suppressed indicates customer request or compliance block; pending_verification indicates awaiting confirmation.

attributes.name: contact_type
attributes.description: The type or category of contact method (e.g., primary email, mobile phone, work phone, WhatsApp, SMS, fax). Determines the channel and priority for omnichannel outreach. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: primary_email|secondary_email|mobile|home_phone|work_phone|whatsapp|sms|fax — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.description: The timestamp when this contact method record was first created in the system. Supports audit trails and data lineage.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which this contact method became active and valid for customer communication. Supports temporal tracking and historical analysis.

attributes.description: The date of the most recent bounce or delivery failure for this contact method. Nullable if no bounces have occurred.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this contact method record was last updated. Supports change tracking and audit trails.

attributes.name: last_used_date
attributes.description: The date when this contact method was last successfully used for customer communication (email sent, SMS delivered, call completed). Helps identify stale or inactive contact points.

attributes.description: Numeric ranking indicating the priority order of this contact method relative to other contact methods for the same customer. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used for fallback logic in omnichannel campaigns.

attributes.description: The unique identifier for this contact method in the source system. Enables traceability and cross-system reconciliation.

attributes.name: value

attributes.name: verification_date
